claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me ask a few more questions about your circumstances.

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now, regarding Alex:

Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards looking after him (for example, on food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to confirm your eligibility:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One final question: Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or residential accommodation, or has he been for an extended period recently?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, he has been in hospital for a while now - a few months. But I still regularly buy things for him like his favorite snacks, toys, and clothes while he's there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. I'm sorry to hear Alex has been in hospital for a while.

Since he's been in hospital for more than 12 weeks (a few months), this is relevant to your eligibility. However, you mentioned that you regularly spend money on him while he's there.

To clarify: When you say you regularly buy things for Alex (snacks, toys, clothes), are these purchases ongoing and consistent throughout his hospital stay? This is important because for children in a UK hospital for more than 12 weeks, you may still be entitled to Child Benefit if you are regularly spending money on them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I've been buying things for him regularly throughout his entire hospital stay. I visit him and bring him his favorite snacks, new toys to keep him entertained, and clothes he needs. It's been consistent the whole time he's been there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. It's lovely that you've been so attentive to Alex during his hospital stay.

Just one more question: Is Alex in a hospital in the UK, or is he receiving treatment abroad?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's in a hospital here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I have good news!

## Eligibility Outcome for Alex

**You appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's a summary of why:

- ✅ Alex is under 16 years old (he's 8)
- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ You are responsible for Alex (he normally lives with you)
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- ✅ Although Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, you qualify for an **exception** because you are regularly spending money on him during his stay (snacks, toys, clothes)

### Important Note

You should inform HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) about Alex's hospital stay if you haven't already. You can do this by filling in an online form or contacting HMRC by phone or post. This ensures your Child Benefit continues correctly while Alex is in hospital.

I hope Alex recovers well soon! Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
